segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, and `TransformStream` are the WHATWG (browser-standard) backbone of pipeline-style data processing. Node has its own, older, differently-shaped `stream` module — see the Node rows below — that real Node code (including `fs`/`http`/`child_process` internally) actually uses far more than the WHATWG API.

Full design: [TDD-00097](../tdd/TDD-00097.md) ([ADR-00296](../adr/ADR-00296.md)–[ADR-00302](../adr/ADR-00302.md), [ADR-00304](../adr/ADR-00304.md)). `pipeTo` (all four shutdown-propagation rules + `prevent*` + `AbortSignal`), `pipeThrough`, and `tee()` come with the rows below; in-memory pipelines run on the promise/microtask runtime alone — no fibers or libcurl. HTTP integration is tracked where it surfaces: fetch `Response.body` on [NETWORKING.md](NETWORKING.md), streaming response/request bodies on [HTTP-SERVER.md](HTTP-SERVER.md).

caveats: No BYOB readers / byte controllers (`type: 'bytes'` rejected at compile time) — byte data flows as `Uint8Array` chunks through default readers
`ReadableStream.from()` accepts arrays only, not async iterables

Source callbacks must be arrow/function-expression/method-shorthand literals; a cancel callback can't take a reason parameter; *async* method shorthand (`{ async pull(c) {…} }`) doesn't parse — use `pull: async (c) => …`
`read()` on a closed stream yields the chunk type's zero value, not `undefined`; `controller.desiredSize` is `0` (not `null`) once closed/errored
`releaseLock()` leaves queued pending reads pending instead of rejecting them
`values()` returns a reader usable in `for await` only (no standalone `.next()`)
In the no-fiber tier, `await` of an already-settled `read()` skips the microtask drain, so a pending pull can run one tick later than real JS
A synchronously-throwing pull/start propagates to the caller instead of erroring the stream
`tee()` forwards the last cancelling branch's reason instead of composing both; a signal abort of `pipeTo` takes effect at the next chunk boundary
notes: One 144-byte heap struct fuses stream + controller + reader (compile-time retyping); chunk queue + pending-read promise FIFO with HWM/size accounting; spec CallPullIfNeeded; per-site fulfill thunk builds typed `{value,done}` records ([ADR-00296](../adr/ADR-00296.md))
Runs on the promise/microtask runtime alone — no fibers or libcurl for in-memory pipelines

caveats: `desiredSize` is `0` (not `null`) once errored; `releaseLock()` doesn't reject a pending-write view
A synchronously-throwing sink write propagates instead of erroring the stream (an async rejection is handled per spec)
A sink abort callback can't take a reason parameter; no transformer/sink `start` promise-vs-write interlock beyond the started flag
notes: 128-byte fused stream+controller+writer struct; 32-byte write-queue entries carry their own per-write promise; `ready` re-armed on backpressure flips ([ADR-00297](../adr/ADR-00297.md))

caveats: No transformer `start` callback
Cancelling the readable side doesn't error the writable side
An identity transform (no callback) requires matching I/O chunk representations
notes: Writable sink write runs the transform when the readable side has capacity, else parks the chunk (at most one, by write serialization); readable pull resumes it; spec defaults writable HWM 1 / readable HWM 0 ([ADR-00298](../adr/ADR-00298.md))

caveats: The format argument must be a string literal ("gzip", "deflate", "deflate-raw") — a runtime-computed format string is a compile error
Chunks are `Uint8Array` only (no ArrayBuffer/DataView BufferSource variants)
notes: A `%kml.ts` TransformStream context with native zlib transform/flush closures; `-lz` linked only when constructed; inflate auto-detects gzip/zlib wrappers ([ADR-00302](../adr/ADR-00302.md))

caveats: Delivers the blob's bytes as a **single** `Uint8Array` chunk (the whole blob), not incrementally chunked as a real byte source would be
notes: Returns a `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` — one owned-copy chunk then closed; an empty blob yields no chunk ([ADR-00341](../adr/ADR-00341.md)). Consumable via `for await` or `.getReader()`

caveats: All five constructors default to **string chunks** (`<T>` overrides — [ADR-00449](../adr/ADR-00449.md); previously `Readable`/`Writable`/`Transform` defaulted to a numeric chunk that silently mangled pushed strings); `new PassThrough()` is the identity Transform, `highWaterMark`/`objectMode` options only ([ADR-00422](../adr/ADR-00422.md)); `new Duplex(...)` accepts only `read`/`write`/`final` callbacks plus the shared options ([ADR-00493](../adr/ADR-00493.md))

`class X extends Readable/Writable/Duplex/Transform` with a `this`-based `_read()` / `_write(chunk, enc, cb)` / `_transform(chunk, enc, cb)` override is supported (a `Duplex` drives both sides independently; a `Transform` routes each write through `_transform`, whose `this.push` feeds the readable side; `<T>` names both chunk types, or `Transform<In, Out>` names each). No `_flush` override yet. Options form (`new Readable({ read })`) also stays
The options-form `read`/`write` callback receives the stream as a parameter, not as `this` (object-literal callbacks have no `this` binding); the class form has the real `this`

`highWaterMark` (options form and class-form `super({ highWaterMark })`) sets the queue watermark; `objectMode` is accepted but has no effect (chunks are already typed by `<T>`, effectively object-mode). A `super(options)` `highWaterMark` must be a literal/construction-scope constant — it can't reference a constructor parameter
A class-form `_write` completion callback is treated as fired when `_write` returns — it can't defer the write past the call
Event names must be string literals; supported events are `data`/`end`/`error`/`close`/`finish`/`drain`

Synchronous `.read([size])` pops one queued chunk (empty → null, size ignored — [ADR-00484](../adr/ADR-00484.md)); `.destroy([err])` closes both sides (the error argument is dropped, no 'error' re-emission) and `.setEncoding('utf8')` is a no-op on the string-chunk default ([ADR-00483](../adr/ADR-00483.md))
Event delivery can lag Node's synchronous re-entrancy by a microtask (emissions ride the reaction queue)
`fs`/`http` still don't hand out Node streams (their surfaces are WHATWG-based or buffered)
notes: Wrappers over the WHATWG internals: rstream/wstream sides + the EventEmitter listener-list runtime; flowing mode is a reaction-driven read→emit loop started by the first `'data'` listener; `Readable.from`/`.fromWeb`/`.toWeb` bridge both worlds ([ADR-00304](../adr/ADR-00304.md))

The class form is a synthetic-root model mirroring `extends EventEmitter`: a hidden Node-stream handle field, the runtime pull/sink routed to the subclass's `_read`/`_write` method ([ADR-00393](../adr/ADR-00393.md))

caveats: The callback forms' callback takes zero parameters or one (the error) — no `(err, value)` extras
`finished(s, cb)` returns nothing, not Node's cleanup function
Function-stage pipelines (`pipeline(src, async function* …)`) are not supported — stages must be streams
notes: Both forms: the `stream/promises` promise-returning ones ([ADR-00304](../adr/ADR-00304.md)) and the callback-style `stream.pipeline(a, b, cb)`/`stream.finished(s, cb)` named exports — a per-site runner on the destination's closed promise calls the callback with `null`/the error; `pipeline`'s callback form returns the destination stream ([ADR-00422](../adr/ADR-00422.md))

caveats: String chunks only (no `<T>` form)
The sides are Duplex *handles* (`write`/`end`/`on`/`pipe`/…), not `Duplex` class instances — no `instanceof Duplex`, `cork`/`uncork`, `.read()`, or `'readable'` events
notes: Two cross-wired identity-transform sides: each side's sink enqueues into the peer's readable (backpressure parks on the peer's capacity); ending one side ends the other's readable. Returned as a 2-element array, so `const [a, b] = duplexPair()` and `pair[0]` both work ([ADR-00422](../adr/ADR-00422.md))
